# Master catalogue — every level-3, distance ≥ 2 factory

Generated from [`master_catalog.json`](master_catalog.json) by
[`catalogfile.py`](catalogfile.py) — **do not edit by hand**; edit
nothing here, run [`merge_results.py`](merge_results.py) instead.
Every row is re-checked against its own columns by
[`verify_catalog.py`](verify_catalog.py).

**1277 distinct `(n, k, d, GL(k,2) gate)` classes**, every one with an
explicit circuit whose gate, check parities, distance, output width,
freedom from spectator and pseudo-outputs, freedom from check wires
that carry no syndrome bit of their own, and — where those are
computable — exact T-count and reduced degree are re-derived from its
columns.

## What this table is, and is not

It is the union of what the repository knows, on one page. It is **not** a
uniform claim: a row's regime says how its class was found and keeps
that claim, because a Pareto point of a classification and a search
witness are different kinds of statement.

| regime | what a row from it means |
|---|---|
| `exhaustive classification n<=54 (Pareto point)` (74 rows) | a Pareto point of the exhaustive classification of generalised triorthogonal protocols through length 54 (classification/length54/): no protocol with n <= 54, the same CNOT+S output class and the same exact distance has n and S both no larger and one of them smaller, where S counts every matrix row -- the N of this table |
| `exhaustive classification n<=54` (105 rows) | found within the exhaustive classification through length 54 but not one of its Pareto points: a Pareto point with the same output class (after removing spectator outputs) and the same exact distance strictly dominates it, which tests/test_master_catalog.py checks -- a verified witness, not an optimum |
| `symmetry-SAT search` (31 rows) | found by the symmetry-slot or ansatz-free SAT search (symmetry_sat_search/); a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `AI search` (371 rows) | found by an AI search campaign; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `AI search: punctured r=7 simplex parents` (19 rows) | found by the 48 < n < 128 AI campaigns, from punctured r=7 simplex parents with free-row appending; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `AI search: multi-agent campaign 39<=n<=127` (95 rows) | found by the 39 <= n <= 127 multi-actor AI campaign (three Opus 5 actors, two conferring Fable 5 reviewers, three rounds, 2026-09-01); a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `AI search (gamma frontier): from Wills parent codes` (73 rows) | built from one of Wills's parent codes (weighted Reed-Muller, restricted-light or one-heavy) by searched punctures, paired-column contractions or logical-pair checks, in the pure-T distillation-exponent release (gamma = log(n/k)/log d, n < 1000); a verified witness, not a maximum -- only the release's own frontier points are the lowest gamma it knows |
| `AI search (gamma frontier): contraction of an existing code` (35 rows) | a paired-column contraction of an existing triorthogonal code, in the pure-T distillation-exponent release (gamma = log(n/k)/log d, n < 1000); a verified witness, not a maximum -- only the release's own frontier points are the lowest gamma it knows |
| `AI search (gamma frontier): logical restriction of a length-54 Pareto point` (11 rows) | a restriction to fewer logical rows of a Pareto point of the length-54 classification, in the pure-T distillation-exponent release (gamma = log(n/k)/log d, n < 1000); a verified witness, not a maximum -- only the release's own frontier points are the lowest gamma it knows |
| `AI search (gamma frontier): punctured Reed-Muller code` (1 rows) | a punctured Reed-Muller code found by the gamma sub-1000 AI campaign (RM(3,10) punctured at 123 points), filed with the pure-T distillation-exponent frontier (gamma = log(n/k)/log d, n < 1000); a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `AI search: Wills downset framework` (2 rows) | verified witness from the 2026-09-14 wills_downset_theory campaign in magic-states-AI, which solved the arXiv:2608.24000 downset framework EXACTLY at every n <= 1000; the d=7 and d=8 rows are proved optima of that framework, not merely best-found, but the framework is one family and they are not maxima over all factories |
| `AI search: pure-T width campaign n=255, 511` (2 rows) | new [[n,k,d]] classes at n=255 and n=511 (the n=511 one the first at d=3 there) -- pure disjoint T^k, verified from columns. NOT rate records: both are strictly dominated by direct sums of the catalogued [[127,23,3]] (rho 5.5217) -- 2 copies give [[254,46,3]] and 4 give [[508,92,3]], each with FEWER inputs and MORE outputs than the row here. Beating the derived baseline needs k>=47 at n=255 and k>=93 at n=511. |
| `AI search: generalised triorthogonal search 55<=n<=64` (79 rows) | found by the AI-assisted public search for generalised triorthogonal protocols at lengths 55-64; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `AI search: pure-T puncture caps` (2 rows) | cap witnesses, NOT records. Each ATTAINS a proved maximum puncture count for its ambient size at d=6, making that bound exact rather than an upper bound: m=8 gives [[248,8,6]] and m=9 gives [[496,16,6]], both with n/t = 31 exactly, hence gamma = log(31)/log(6) = 1.9165 independent of m. Filed as evidence that these cells are closed, not as frontier points -- the d=6 pure-T bar is gamma 1.063146. |
| `AI search: full-simplex pure-T frames` (2 rows) | widest pure-T frames held at n=511. DOMINATED on rate by the derived direct-sum baseline [[508,92,3]] = 4 x [[127,23,3]], rho = 508/92 = 5.5217. These are WIDTH points, explicitly NOT rate records: beating the baseline at n=511 needs k >= 93. |
| `AI search: graph gluing` (9 rows) | found by an AI search that glues catalogued small factories along a graph of paired-column contractions; exact distance verified from columns; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `borrowed-identity search: two-group` (391 rows) | found by the two-group borrowed-identity search of Singh, Gidney and Jones (arXiv:2606.28518; borrowed_identities/): an identity circuit symmetric within its output and check blocks, with its output-only gates removed; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `borrowed-identity search: symmetry-free` (36 rows) | found by the symmetry-free, targeted-output borrowed-identity search of Singh, Gidney and Jones (arXiv:2606.28518; borrowed_identities/), which solves for the check couplings of a chosen output; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `Jain-Albert doubling: weak triply even family` (13 rows) | a code of the weak triply even family of Jain and Albert (arXiv:2408.12752, Table II; transversal_t_codes/): quadratic-residue CSS codes doubled onto [[95,1,7]], rebuilt here from the paper's construction, where T on some qubits and T-dagger on the rest is a logical T; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `Jain-Albert doubling: triorthogonal family` (12 rows) | a code of the triorthogonal family of Jain and Albert (arXiv:2408.12752, Table I; transversal_t_codes/), self-dual CSS codes doubled onto [[95,1,7]], rebuilt here from the paper's construction; a verified witness, not a maximum |
| `borrowed-identity search: SAT recovery` (2 rows) | found by the SAT stage of the unified borrowed-identity search of Singh, Gidney and Jones (arXiv:2606.28518; borrowed_identities/), asked for a factory below the circuit size the other stages reach; a verified witness, not a maximum |

A **class** is `(n, k, d, gate)` with the gate taken up to an invertible
change of the output basis (a CNOT frame, `GL(k,2)`) and diagonal Clifford
corrections — the CNOT+S output equivalence. Circuits at the same
distance whose gates differ only by such a frame, for example `T0·T1` and
`T0·CS01`, are one row; circuits at different distances are always
different rows. The stored circuit is one representative, and `gate` is
exactly what it deposits.

A class found in more than one corpus, or in more than one frame, is **one
row** here, with every contributing source listed in its `sources` field;
the retained circuit is the one with the fewest ambient qubits. `regimes`
therefore tells you the strongest claim available for that class.

`discovery` says whether a class is **found only by AI search**: **633** rows are
`AI search` — found only by AI search campaigns — and **644** are
`pre-existing` — a classification stage run in this repository, the
symmetry-SAT search, the borrowed-identity searches or a community
contribution has them, or the length-54 classification alone does. A
class both an AI search and the length-54
classification found is `AI search`. Whether a class was new to the
literature is what `citation` says, not `discovery`.

Level-2 and level-4 circuits are outside this table by definition: they
use a different rotation angle. So are distance-1 circuits, which detect
no single fault, and padded circuits — a `k` that counts an output the
gate never touches, or two outputs that are the same logical qubit modulo
the check span. `merge_results.py` rejects all four with the reason
printed, and `verify_catalog.py` would reject any that ever got in.
Distance-2 rows are in: the length-54 classification covers `d ≥ 3`
only, so its claims, and the `exhaustive classification` regimes, say
nothing about them.

`T` is the exact minimal level-3 T-count (Amy–Mosca / Reed–Muller
minimum-weight `Z_8` coset); `deg` is the CNOT-frame-reduced
phase-polynomial degree. Both are exact minimisations over groups that
stop being finite in practice past `k = 6`, so above that they are blank
rather than estimated. A `d` marked `≥` is a proved floor, not a
measured distance. `cert d` is a distance the row's source certifies
where this folder could only prove the floor; it is not re-measured
here, and a `≥` there means the source certifies only a lower bound.

`Clifford` says what the circuit needs besides its rotations to deposit
exactly the gate shown (`T = diag(1, e^{iπ/4})`, `CS`, `CCZ`): `none`;
`T-powers` — no Clifford gate, if some rotations run as `T³`, `T⁵` or
`T†` instead of `T` (a transversal `T` in the sense of Jain and Albert);
or `S, CZ` — `S`/`CZ` gates after the rotations, whatever their powers.
Each circuit's own correction is listed with it below.

`citation` names the papers that credit the class. A class in the
published literature is credited to the earliest work that published it,
linked; a class the Borrowed Identities searches (Singh, Gidney and Jones)
were the first to publish, to that paper; a class a community
contribution brought, to its contributor's work; every other class, to
the length-54 classification and/or the symmetry-and-AI report. Full
entries are under [References](#references).

## Circuits

Columns are the qubit supports of each parity-`T` rotation; qubits
`0..k-1` are the outputs, the rest are postselected checks. Every circuit
is stored in its `S_k`-canonical output frame, so these columns deposit
exactly the `gate` shown — the rows too wide to canonicalise say so.

Circuits with more than 200 columns are **not** printed
here: a thousand-column list is not something a reader reads, and
inlining them would triple this file to no purpose. They are complete in
[`master_catalog.json`](master_catalog.json), which is the machine-
readable copy of exactly these rows.

### 1. `[[8,3,2]]` — CCZ012

- output gate: `012`
- `N = 4` (3 outputs + 1 check), exact minimal T-count 7, reduced degree 3
- distance: exactly 2, witnessed by the fault on columns [0, 1]
- leading error coefficient: `A_2 = 28` accepted harmful faults of weight 2
- Clifford correction, every rotation a `T`: `Z on 0`, `Z on 1`, `Z on 2`, `CZ on (0,1)`, `CZ on (0,2)`, `CZ on (1,2)`
